biography: Walter Corsi, born in the bustling favelas of São Paulo, Brazil, didn't have a silver spoon. His racing journey began with go-karts cobbled together from scrap parts, tearing around makeshift tracks with the raw hunger to compete and escape his surroundings. He honed his skills at Interlagos, the same hallowed ground where his idols Senna and Fittipaldi made history. Corsi's aggressive style quickly gained attention, attracting the eye of Tepetes Bandeirante, a prominent Brazilian racing team. One defining moment was his stunning last-lap overtake at the Curitiba Grand Prix in 2021, a move that cemented his reputation as a fearless driver. Now at 33, Corsi is considered to be at his peak, battling for championships and carrying the hopes of a nation yearning for another racing hero.
drivingStyle: Corsi is a relentlessly aggressive driver, known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the limits. He attacks every corner with unmatched intensity, often threading the needle through tight gaps. While his tire management skills are not his strongest suit, he compensates with sheer speed and relentless pressure on his opponents. He thrives in high-pressure situations, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest. He is often criticized for his occasional over-aggressiveness but that is part of what makes him successful.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their early karting days, where they frequently clashed. Vargas accuses Corsi of unsportsmanlike conduct, while Corsi dismisses Vargas as simply being unable to handle the pressure.

A fierce on-track battle for position at the 2022 Interlagos Grand Prix led to a controversial collision, resulting in both drivers retiring. Tensions have remained high ever since, with each accusing the other of reckless driving.
Tanaka openly questions Corsi's tactics, referring to him as overly aggressive and dangerous. They have had multiple run-ins on track, often resulting in damaged cars and post-race confrontations.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of socks that his grandmother gave him before every race, no matter how tattered they become.
Listens to a specific samba song, 'Brasil Pandeiro', on repeat in the moments before getting into the car, as a way to connect with his roots and center himself.
Always traces a cross on his steering wheel before the start of the race, a habit he picked up from his deeply religious mother.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about finesse; it's about heart. If you're not willing to risk everything, you're not willing to win."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2023 Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos, fulfilling a lifelong dream and sending the home crowd into a frenzy. He fought off intense pressure from multiple world champions to secure the victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the 2020 Monaco Grand Prix due to a mechanical failure. The heartbreak was palpable, as he had dominated the race and victory seemed certain.
